A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the impact of experience on risk judgments is mediated by a number of other psychological factors, including personality, and is not as simple as the “psychometric paradigm” suggests.
experience of risk activities is an important variable in explaining individual differences in risk judgments, but the nature of that relationship is complex.
experience is a key factor in risk perception and should be included in any model of risk perception.
The main takeaway from our work is that
risk perceptions are influenced by a range of different factors.
risk perceptions are not a function of personality but of risk experiences.
experience of risk is not a single construct but a complex set of variables which are likely to have different relationships with risk perceptions in voluntary and involuntary risk situations.
